facts.fact: The government's commemorative account says the Birth, Marriage and Death department has sat within the Ministry of Home Affairs since 2009 and that the civil registration and identity systems were 'automated' over time, under a Civil Registration Act of 2023 that replaced the 1986 law; it dates none of the automation, so the page's published date of 14 April 2026 (itself a proxy) is used.

systems.tiers: said to have been automated over time, with no statement of where entry is made; birth, marriage and death registration extended into several Tinkhundla centres

registration offices within health facilities, registering newborns there, in Mbabane, Piggs Peak, Mankayane, Hlathikhulu, Sithobelweni, Manzini and Siteki (7); whether the entry is digital is not stated
nationwide, taking registration into chiefdoms; over 30,000 people given first birth certificates
